title: Modular CI builders, dependency lifecycle gardener, and quiet release handoff
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Refactors CI into modular builders; adds a dependency lifecycle gardener that tracks shrinkwrap/lockfile drift and introduces a quiet release handoff script to reduce noisy rollouts. No user-facing API changes.
commits: init: split ci-builder into language-agnostic modules
feat(dep-gardener): add lifecycle controller and dry-run report generator
chore: move legacy-lint-wrapper into deprecated/ and add shim
ci: preserve shrinkwrap during ephemeral runner cleanup
docs: ci migration guide and rollout checklist
fix(release): ensure quiet-handoff respects pending deploy windows
description:
Context: Our monolithic CI bootstrap and release handoff scripts have accumulated special-cases for language toolchains and ad-hoc dependency updates. This causes long presubmit startup times, noisy release windows when lockfiles drift, and brittle release automation during high-traffic deploys.

Motivation: Break the CI surface into small, composable builders (images + entrypoints) that can be shared across repos and runtime types; introduce a dependency lifecycle gardener that performs lightweight drift detection, produces dry-run recommendations, and exports telemetry; and add a quiet release handoff that sequences webhook-based releases to avoid cascading throttles. The goal is improved presubmit latency, clearer dep-change windows, and safer automated releases.

What this PR does (summary):
- Modularizes CI: moves language/tool-specific steps into .github/builders/{node,python,go,rust} and introduces a top-level runner that composes builders based on changed paths.
- Adds tools/dep-gardener/: a Go utility and a lightweight cron action that inspects lockfiles (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, go.sum), compares them to the canonical shrinkwrap in infra/, and emits a dry-run report with suggestions (upgrade path, transitive risk).
- Preserves transient shrinkwrap state across ephemeral CI runners to reduce unnecessary churn when quick dependency refreshes happen.
- Introduces scripts/release/quiet-handoff.sh which gates release webhooks on an opt-in quiet window and can annotate Linear items for follow-up.
- Deprecates legacy-lint-wrapper: moves it to tools/deprecated/ and adds a shim that adapts old teams to the new builder interface.
- Adds docs/ci-migration.md describing the migration steps and rollback guidance.

Checklist: 
- [x] Modular CI builders implemented and unit-tested locally
- [x] Dep-gardener dry-run report implemented, prints machine-parsable JSON and human summary
- [x] Release handoff script with integration tests in a local harness
- [x] Migration guide and rollout checklist included
- [x] Telemetry: dep-gardener emits metric keys compatible with existing CI telemetry (ci.dep_gardener.dryrun.count, ci.dep_gardener.alerts)

Files touched (high level):
- .github/builders/{node.yml,python.yml,go.yml,rust.yml} - new modular builder actions
- .github/workflows/ci-composer.yml - orchestrates composed builders based on changed paths
- tools/dep-gardener/main.go, Dockerfile, README.md - lockfile diff and report generator
- scripts/release/quiet-handoff.sh - quiet release gate script
- tools/deprecated/legacy-lint-wrapper.sh - shim and deprecation note
- docs/ci-migration.md - migration and rollback steps
- infra/shrinkwrap/ - canonical lockfile placement (small metadata changes)

Testing and verification:
- Local runner: validated modular builders run in isolation, preserved runtime env across Node/Python switchcases.
- Dep-gardener: ran dry-run on multiple repos with small/medium lockfile deltas to ensure no false positives; added unit tests for comparator.
- E2E: executed quiet-handoff in a staging project: verified the handoff respects opt-in flags and delays webhook delivery by configured window.
- CI: initial run failed on lint due to legacy wrapper assumptions; addressed by adding compatibility shim and rerunning; final CI status: pass.

Review conversation (excerpt):
- Miguel Torres: "Nice split. Can dep-gardener run as a presubmit job only for PRs that touch lockfiles? We should avoid adding noise to PRs that only touch docs."
  - Asha: "Agreed — implemented a path filter and now the action short-circuits unless lockfile paths are changed (or CI is explicitly triggered). Added the filter to ci-composer.yml."
- Eve Zhang: "Telemetry keys look fine but add a low-cardinality label for repo and a hash of changes so we can correlate recurrent churn."
  - Asha: "Added repo label and a stable short-hash in the report; updated README to explain retention and PII considerations."
- Connor Lee: "Compatibility shim looks okay, but please ensure we document to deprecate the wrapper in two release cycles."
  - Asha: "Added timeline to docs/ci-migration.md and created a linear task (ENG-8967) for follow-up automation to remove the shim after two cycles."

CI summary: initial run: fail (legacy-lint-wrapper path), addressed by shim; subsequent runs: pass on all matrix entries. Lint and unit tests green; no flaky integration failures observed during multiple reruns.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature-flagged rollout gates for teams that opt in to modular builders.
2) Enable dep-gardener dry-run in all repos for two weeks (no auto remediation) and export telemetry for evaluation.
3) After one cycle of observed reductions in presubmit churn, enable advisory alerts to PR authors.
4) After two cycles, remove legacy shim and fully deprecate legacy wrapper.

Compatibility notes: This change does not alter public SDKs or runtime APIs. It modifies CI infra and release automation only. The dep-gardener produces advisory reports; it does not auto-commit or change lockfiles in this PR.

Merge: squash and merge. Post-merge tasks: schedule three rolling-hour quiet windows for initial release handoff and add a short playbook entry for on-call in docs/ci-migration.md.
notes: Follow-up: ENG-8967 will track shim removal and automation
